newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Soekor, govt signs oil exploration deal.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Soekor, govt signs oil exploration deal.

text.p: South Africa on Tuesday signed a major offshore oil exploration deal which marked the re-entry of foreign companies into South African offshore exploration after nearly two decades.
A subsidiary of U.S.-based Phillips Petroleum Inc signed an agreement to join three other companies in exploring a 14.5 million acre block off South Africa's east coast.
The subsidiary, Phillips Petroleum South Africa Ltd, will operate the sub-lease with a 40 percent interest.
Canada's PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, and South Africa's Energy Africa Ltd and Sasol Ltd each hold a 20 percent interest in the exploration sub lease.
The initial four-year agreement was signed for South Africa by Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuel Maduna and state-owned oil exploration company Soekor.
The exploration area extends from the Mozambique border to just south of the Indian Ocean port city of Durban.
Soekor said in a statement that the sub-lease gave the partners the exclusive right to explore for natural oil and gas.
Phillips said in a separate statement that under the agreement it will gather 1,500 km of seismic data and drill at least one exploratory well.
The company said it was committed to spending $8 million in the first four years while the agreement may be extended for two periods of three years each.
Soekor and Phillips signed a technical agreement in March last year granting the U.S. company the exclusive right to evaluate the oil and gas potential in the area.
Soekor said in April the Phillips deal is seen as a major breakthrough for the South African oil company and could entice other oil companies to South Africa's waters.
